verdicts.claim: By default SQLite runs an automatic checkpoint when a COMMIT leaves the WAL at 1000 pages or more, and also when the last connection closes
verdicts.evidence: wal.html 3.1: 'automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size, or when the last database connection on a database file closes'; pragma.html: wal_autocheckpoint default 1000.

verdicts.claim: Automatic checkpoints and sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() run in PASSIVE mode, which copies as many frames as it can without waiting for readers or writers
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE'; C API: passive 'might leave the checkpoint unfinished'.

verdicts.claim: SQLite defines four checkpoint modes. PASSIVE does not wait. FULL waits until no writer is active and all readers use the latest snapshot
verdicts.evidence: Mode descriptions match, but the count is wrong: C API lists a fifth valid mode, 'SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP — This mode always checkpoints zero frames'; pragma.html also lists wal_checkpoint(NOOP).

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE never invokes the busy-handler callback. FULL, RESTART, and TRUNCATE invoke it while they wait for the writer lock and for readers
verdicts.evidence: C API: 'busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode'; 'If any other process is running a checkpoint ... SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked'.

verdicts.claim: A checkpoint must stop at the first WAL page past the end mark of any current reader. It resumes from that point on the next run
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'checkpoint must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader ... will resume ... from where it left off'; rewind only 'if the entire WAL has been transferred ... synced and if no readers are making use of the WAL'.

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) truncates the WAL file to zero bytes when it completes successfully. A PASSIVE checkpoint does not shrink the physical -wal file
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: TRUNCATE 'WAL file is truncated to zero bytes upon successful completion'; 'in WAL mode, the write-ahead log file is not truncated following a checkpoint'; PhotoStructure: 'PASSIVE doesn't TRUNCATE'. Caveat: journal_size_limit can truncate on reset.

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE never shrinks the physical -wal file; only TRUNCATE does. (Overview)
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html journal_size_limit: 'Each time a transaction is committed or a WAL file resets ... if the journal or WAL file is larger it is truncated to the limit.' So TRUNCATE is not the only way the -wal file shrinks.

verdicts.claim: SQLite's WAL page lists three causes: automatic checkpointing disabled, checkpoint starvation from overlapping readers, and very large write
verdicts.evidence: wal.html bullets: 'Disabling the automatic checkpoint mechanism', 'Checkpoint starvation' ('always at least one active reader ... WAL file will grow without bound'), 'Very large write transactions'.

verdicts.claim: A long-lived read transaction holds back checkpoint progress ... A Syncthing thread reports a transaction open for hours blocking WAL cleanup
verdicts.evidence: Syncthing: 'If a transaction is open for hours, we can't remove pages written to the WAL after its start'; wal.html: 'a long-running read transaction can prevent a checkpointer from making progress'.

verdicts.claim: Syncthing reports its WAL growing to multiple gigabytes while the checkpointer waits for such a window
verdicts.evidence: Cited post only says, conditionally, 'If the size of the WAL reaches critical levels of multiple gigabytes, we need to act' (no observed size); linked GitHub issue #10559 gives no sizes. A WebSearch snippet points to an uncited Syncthing thread (26082) reporting 41-200 GiB WALs, not fetched.

notes: All six cited URLs were cache hits with text; 1 WebFetch (github.com/syncthing/syncthing/issues/10559) and 1 WebSearch were used.
